paper_title: Estimating the Effect of Unearned Income on Labor Earnings, Savings, and Consumption
paper_citation: Imbens, G. W., Rubin, D. B., & Sacerdote, B. I. (2001). AER 91(4): 778–794.
user_message: Replicate the reduced-form elasticity of labor earnings with respect to yearly lottery prize for modest prizes (Table 2 / paper discussion; benchmark ≈ −0.11 in this JSON). Use data.csv columns yearlpr (prize) and yearn.1–yearn.7 (post-win earnings by year). Do not substitute the big-winner dummy or Table 5 level specification unless you document why this reference is wrong.
model_notes: Reduced-form: post-winning labor earnings on yearlpr. yearn.1 = win year (t=0); yearn.2–yearn.7 = years 1–6 after win; xearn.1–xearn.6 = pre-win earnings. Modest-prize subsamples often use winner==1 and bigwinner==0 (194 obs); controls are winner==0 (259). Construct the outcome to match Table 2 (e.g. average post-win earnings or log specification) before comparing to the published elasticity.

data_source.sample: 259 controls (small one-time prizes), 237 major-prize winners (43 bigwinner, 194 small winners)

data_columns.yearlpr: Annual lottery prize amount (yearly payment for annuity prizes).
data_columns.yearn.2: Labor earnings, one year after win (t=1).
data_columns.yearn.3: Labor earnings, two years after win (t=2).
data_columns.yearn.4: Labor earnings, three years after win (t=3).
data_columns.yearn.5: Labor earnings, four years after win (t=4).
data_columns.yearn.6: Labor earnings, five years after win (t=5).
data_columns.yearn.7: Labor earnings, six years after win (t=6).
data_columns.xearn.1: Pre-win earnings, six years before win.
data_columns.xearn.6: Pre-win earnings, one year before win.
data_columns.winner: 1 if won a major Megabucks prize; 0 if control (small prize only).
data_columns.bigwinner: 1 if big winner (43); among winners, 0 with winner==1 is small winner (194).
